subject: dsa
title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
summary: Breadth-first search with a queue. Process the whole current level at once, recording its values and enqueuing the next level's children.
problem: Return the node values level by level, top to bottom, grouped into one list per level.

steps.caption: We want the values grouped by depth. Depth-first recursion mixes levels, so use breadth-first search with a queue instead.
Seed the queue with the root. Whatever the queue holds right now is one full level — the first level is just [3].
Record [3], then enqueue its children. The queue now holds the next whole level: [9, 20].
Record [9, 20] and enqueue their children. 9 has none; 20 adds 15 and 7. Next level: [15, 7].
Record [15, 7] — both are leaves, so nothing new is enqueued and the queue empties. Levels top to bottom: [[3], [9, 20], [15, 7]].
